_comment: Logging configuration for the deployed web service, passed to uvicorn as
--log-config. It ships inside the release tree, so it is versioned with the
code it configures.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS.
The hardening middleware writes one compact JSON object per request to the
'vmr.http' logger, and writes sanitized exception events to it as well.
Nothing in the application configures logging - deliberately, because
logging configuration is a deployment concern - and uvicorn's built-in
config declares only the 'uvicorn', 'uvicorn.error' and 'uvicorn.access'
loggers, with no root entry. So under a plain `uvicorn app.main:app` the
root logger keeps its default WARNING level and has no handler: every
'vmr.http' INFO record is discarded before it reaches journald. The
observability contract documented in docs/PRODUCTION_HARDENING.md would be
silently absent on the server, and the absence looks exactly like a quiet
system.
This config keeps uvicorn's own loggers exactly as uvicorn defines them and
adds one more: 'vmr' at INFO, on its own stdout handler, propagate false so
the records are not duplicated. The formatter is the bare message, because
the application already emits a complete JSON object - wrapping it in a
second layer of formatting would make it unparseable.
journald receives it via StandardOutput=journal. Read it with:
journalctl -u vmr-web -o cat | grep '"event":"http_request"'
